subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: Should a native relay failure with no matching current tool-call invocation fall through to normal OpenClaw before-tool policy for every approval mode?
rationale: Tests show the branch preserves post-invocation fail-closed behavior, but only an owner can confirm that generic policy evaluation is an acceptable security-equivalent fallback when native relay transport is unavailable.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback after proof
options.body: Accept the pre-invocation fallback after exact-head restart proof shows both successful recovery and preserved policy denial.

options.title: Require relay-only recovery
options.body: Keep approval fail-closed and repair or regenerate the relay registration before allowing the tool request to proceed.

options.title: Pause pending boundary redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until native relay and app-server approval ownership can be consolidated into one canonical recovery path.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the pre-invocation fallback after exact-head restart proof shows both successful recovery and preserved policy denial.

likelyOwner.reason: The neighboring guarded unavailable behavior was merged through their current-main work, making them the strongest available owner for this boundary decision.
